drugs.name: Varenicline

receptors.clinicalAction: Active modulation of Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor contributes to clinical efficacy and tolerability.

adverseFootprint.description: Risk rating: Very Low (No Excess vs Plb)

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 0.5 mg PO Once Daily with Food
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer in the morning with a full glass of water and substantial meal to prevent nausea. Patient continues smoking normally as receptors pre- load.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Advance to 0.5 mg BID. Patient sets Target Quit Date (TQD) for Day 8. Cigarettes begin tasting unrewarding and flat due to competitive nAChR blockade.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.dose: Target Quit Date & Full Maintenance (Day 8 to Week 12)
titrationSchedule.timing: 1.0 mg PO Twice Daily with Meals
titrationSchedule.directive: Patient stops smoking completely on Day 8. Take 1.0 mg morning and 1.0 mg dinner. If nausea is intolerable, reduce dose to 0.5 mg BID without sacrificing efficacy.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: 1.0 mg PO BID for Additional 12 Weeks
titrationSchedule.directive: In patients successfully abstinent at Week 12, an additional 12-week course significantly prevents long-term relapse. Renal failure (< 30 mL/min): max 0.5 mg BID. BLACK BOX WARNING & CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATIONS • Removal of FDA Black Box Warning (EAGLES Consensus): In 2016, the FDA removed the neuropsychiatric black box warning following the definitive 8,000-patient EAGLES trial proving safety across psychiatric cohorts. • Seizure Risk: Rare post-marketing seizures reported; use caution in patients with pre-existing epilepsy. • Accidental Alcohol Intolerance: Some patients report increased drunkenness, aggressive behavior, or amnesia when combining varenicline with alcohol; advise moderation.

clinicalPearls: The 'Full Glass of Water' Anti-Nausea Pearl: Nausea is the most common reason for varenicline discontinuation (affecting ~ 30%). Instruct patients to NEVER swallow the tablet on an empty stomach. Taking varenicline strictly after a substantial meal with an entire 250 mL glass of water decreases nausea by > 70%.

Why Smoking Continues During Week 1: Crucially explain to the patient that they are EXPECTED to smoke during Days 1 to 7. Pre-saturating the receptors while smoking causes inhaled nicotine to lose its punch; patients spontaneously notice cigarettes taste 'like burning paper' before their Target Quit Date arrives.

The Landmark EAGLES Trial: The EAGLES trial enrolled 8,144 smokers (half with severe psychiatric disorders including schizophrenia, bipolar, and major depression). Varenicline demonstrated superior quit rates over bupropion and nicotine patches with zero increase in suicidal thoughts, depression, or aggression compared to placebo.

drugs.name: Bupropion SR

receptors.clinicalAction: Inhibits DAT in nucleus accumbens; boosts tonic dopamine, replacing nicotine-evoked dopamine release and relieving withdrawal.
Directly blocks nicotinic ion channels; attenuates the reinforcing reward of smoking if the patient slips and smokes a cigarette.
Zero serotonergic reuptake inhibition; zero risk of sexual dysfunction, emotional blunting, or weight gain.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Screen History of Seizures / Eating Disorders Screen for absolute contraindications: history of seizures, active or past bulimia/anorexia nervosa, and abrupt discontinuation of alcohol or benzodiazepines.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer 150 mg SR tablet in the morning. Smoking continues normally during this phase to establish steady-state hydroxybupropion concentrations.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.dose: Target Escalation & Quit Date Setting (Day 4 to Week 12)
titrationSchedule.directive: Escalate to 150 mg BID. Space doses at least 8 hours apart (e.g. 8 AM and 4 PM) to avoid insomnia. Set Target Quit Date (TQD) between Day 8 and Day 14.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: Continue 150 mg BID for 7 to 12 Weeks
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard treatment duration is 7 to 12 weeks; may extend up to 6 months in patients with persistent craving. Tapering is not strictly required but minimizes rebound fatigue. BLACK BOX WARNING & CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATIONS • SEIZURE DISORDER CONTRAINDICATION: Dose-dependent reduction in seizure threshold; strictly contraindicated in epilepsy, active/history of bulimia or anorexia nervosa, and CNS tumors! • MAO Inhibitor Lethal Clash: Contraindicated within 14 days of MAOIs due to catastrophic hypertensive crisis risk. • Abrupt Alcohol/Sedative Withdrawal: Never initiate during abrupt withdrawal from alcohol, benzodiazepines, or antiepileptics.

clinicalPearls: The '8-Hour Spacing' Insomnia Rule: Bupropion SR is an activating dopaminergic agent. Taking the second daily dose too late in the evening causes severe sleep-onset insomnia. Instruct patients to take the first dose at 8:00 AM and the second dose strictly by 4:00 PM (maintaining the mandatory 8-hour gap to prevent seizure peaks while protecting sleep).

Combating Post-Cessation Weight Gain: The average smoker gains 4 to 6 kg after quitting due to decreased metabolic rate and snacking. Bupropion is the only smoking cessation pharmacotherapy proven to delay and suppress post-cessation weight gain, making it the premier choice for weight-conscious individuals.

Comorbid Depression and Smoking: Approximately 40% of chronic heavy smokers have comorbid major depressive disorder or dysthymia. Bupropion uniquely treats both the underlying depressive episode and nicotine dependence simultaneously with a single medication.

drugs.name: Nicotine Replacement

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Smokers using > 10 cigarettes/day or smoking within 30 min of waking require Step 1 high-dose therapy: 21 mg/24h patch PLUS 4 mg acute oral rescue.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 21 mg/24h Patch + 2–4 mg Lozenge PRN Apply one 21 mg patch every morning to clean, dry, hairless skin. Use one 2 mg or 4 mg lozenge/gum every 1–2 hours PRN for acute breakthrough cravings (max 20/day).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: 14 mg/24h Patch + Continue PRN Lozenge Step down transdermal patch strength to 14 mg/24h while maintaining PRN acute oral rescue. Rotate patch application sites daily (upper arm, chest, back) to prevent erythema.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: 7 mg/24h Patch + Taper Oral Rescue Step down to 7 mg/24h patch for final 2 weeks. Discontinue patch at Week 10; keep acute lozenges/gum on hand for high-risk craving situations for up to 3 to 6 months. CRITICAL CLINICAL CAUTIONS & CARDIOVASCULAR SAFETY • Acute Post-MI Safety: In the immediate post-acute coronary syndrome window (< 2 weeks) or unstable angina, initiate under cardiology guidance (though NRT remains vastly safer than continuing cigarette smoking!). • Chew-and-Park Gum Technique: Chewing nicotine gum vigorously like ordinary chewing gum releases nicotine into saliva where it is swallowed, causing nausea, hiccups, and near-zero absorption! • Pediatric & Pet Toxicity: Used patches still contain substantial residual nicotine; dispose safely away from children and pets.

clinicalPearls: The 'Dual NRT' Imperative: Monotherapy with nicotine patches fails in over 70% of patients because a patch provides flat baseline levels but CANNOT respond to acute craving spikes (after meals, with coffee, during stress). Combining a basal patch (21 mg) with an acute rescue form (2 mg or 4 mg lozenge/gum) doubles long-term cessation rates.

The 'Chew-and-Park' Technique for Gum: Instruct patients to chew the gum slowly until they feel a tingling or peppery taste, then immediately 'PARK' it between the cheek and gum for 15–20 minutes to allow transmucosal absorption. Once tingling fades, chew again and re-park.

Acidity Destroys Oral Absorption: Nicotine requires a neutral to slightly basic salivary pH for mucosal absorption. Acidic beverages (coffee, sodas, orange juice, beer) destroy absorption; instruct patients to consume ONLY water for 15 minutes before and during use of gum or lozenges.

receptors.clinicalAction: Active modulation of Ryanodine Receptor 1 (RyR1) contributes to clinical efficacy and tolerability.
Uncouples electrical action potentials from mechanical muscle contraction without depressing central respiration or cardiac

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Discontinue Neuroleptic + Active Cooling Halt offending antipsychotic immediately. Initiate aggressive external cooling (ice packs, cooled IV fluids) and secure airway. Draw baseline CK, electrolytes, and renal panel.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 1.0 to 2.5 mg/kg Rapid IV Push Administer 1.0 to 2.5 mg/kg rapid IV push via large-bore peripheral or central line. Ryanodex: 1 vial (250 mg) dissolved in 5 mL sterile water. Dantrium: reconstitute with 60 mL water/vial.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.dose: Serial Boluses to Reverse Rigidity (Minutes 15 to 60)
titrationSchedule.directive: Repeat 1.0 mg/kg q15m (Max 10 mg/kg) Repeat boluses every 15 minutes until muscle rigidity resolves, core body temperature normalizes, and heart rate stabilizes. If no response at cumulative 10 mg/kg, reconsider diagnosis.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: 1.0 mg/kg IV q6h (or 100 mg PO QID) Continue maintenance therapy for 24 to 48 hours post-resolution to prevent rebound hyperthermia. Transition to oral dantrolene (100–200 mg/ day divided) or Bromocriptine before stopping. BLACK BOX WARNING & CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATIONS • FATAL HEPATOTOXICITY (BOXED WARNING): High risk of fulminant hepatic necrosis with chronic oral therapy (exceeding 800 mg/day or > 60 days); monitor baseline and frequent transaminases. • Extravasation Tissue Necrosis: Reconstituted solution is highly alkaline (pH 9.5); extravasation causes severe chemical cellulitis, tissue necrosis, and sloughing. • Calcium Channel Blocker Clash: Concomitant IV calcium channel blockers (Verapamil, Diltiazem) with IV dantrolene is strictly contraindicated (provokes fatal hyperkalemia and myocardial collapse!).

clinicalPearls: Ryanodex vs Classical Dantrium Reconstitution: Classical Dantrium (20 mg vials) requires 60 mL of sterile water per vial; resuscitating an 80 kg patient requires reconstituting 10 to 12 bulky vials, consuming 20–30 critical minutes. Ryanodex formulated with nanocrystal technology contains 250 mg in a single vial reconstituted in just 5 mL of water in under 1 minute!

Peripheral Temperature Termination: Fever in Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome and Malignant Hyperthermia is NOT hypothalamic; it is driven entirely by peripheral muscular hypermetabolism. Dantrolene terminates the heat production at the source (the muscle fiber), reversing hyperthermia within 15–30 minutes.

The Dual NMS Rescue Combination: Dantrolene acts purely in the periphery (at RyR1 in muscle), while Bromocriptine acts centrally (at D2 receptors in the striatum and hypothalamus). Combining IV Dantrolene with oral/NG Bromocriptine attacks NMS from both ends, significantly reducing mortality compared to monotherapy.

receptors.clinicalAction: Competitively blocks 5-HT2A receptors in hypothalamus, brainstem, and spinal cord; terminates clonus, tremor, and malignant
Antagonizes 5-HT1A receptors; blunts central hyper-adrenergic agitation, autonomic shivering, and panic.
Exerts profound central antihistaminic sedation; calms severe agitation and blunts sympathetic autonomic outflow.

adverseFootprint.description: Risk rating: High / Very Common (H1 Effect)

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Stop All Serotonergic Drugs + IV Benzos Halt SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, TCAs, Tramadol, and Linezolid immediately. Administer IV Lorazepam (2–4 mg) to control autonomic storm and motor agitation.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 12 mg PO or Crushed via NG Tube Administer 12 mg (three 4 mg tablets) crushed in water down a nasogastric or orogastric tube if patient is confused or obtunded. Rapidly saturates central 5-HT2A sites.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.dose: Serial Re-Dosing for Persistent Clonus (Hours 1 to 6)
titrationSchedule.directive: 2 mg PO/NG q2h PRN Ongoing Clonus If ocular/ankle clonus, tremor, or autonomic instability persists after 2 hours, administer 2 mg every 2 hours until objective clinical stabilization occurs.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: 4 to 8 mg PO/NG q6h for 24 to 48 Hours
titrationSchedule.directive: Continue 4–8 mg q6h for 24 to 48 hours to prevent recrudescence as long-acting serotonergic drugs clear. Do not exceed maximum 32 mg in a 24-hour period. CRITICAL CLINICAL CAUTIONS & RESUSCITATION HAZARDS • NO PARENTERAL FORMULATION (CRITICAL ROUTE BARRIER): Cyproheptadine is strictly an oral/enteral medication; comatose or intubated patients require crushed tablets via NG tube. • Do Not Rely on Monotherapy in Extreme Hyperthermia: When core body temp > 39°C, cyproheptadine alone is insufficient; immediate neuromuscular paralysis (Vecuronium) and intubation are mandatory. • Antipyretics are Completely Ineffective: Acetaminophen and NSAIDs fail because fever is driven by peripheral muscular contractions, not hypothalamic set- point alteration!

clinicalPearls: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria: The gold-standard bedside diagnosis requires the presence of a serotonergic drug PLUS one of the following: (1) Spontaneous clonus; (2) Inducible clonus WITH agitation or diaphoresis; (3) Ocular clonus WITH agitation or diaphoresis; (4) Tremor AND hyperreflexia; (5) Hypertonia AND temperature > 38°C WITH ocular or inducible clonus.

The Nasogastric Administration Pearl: Because severe serotonin syndrome causes agitation and confusion, patients cannot swallow tablets safely. Crush three 4 mg tablets (12 mg) into fine powder, suspend in 30 mL of sterile water, flush down the NG tube, and clamp for 30 minutes to ensure absorption.

Distinguishing Serotonin Syndrome from NMS: Look at the eyes and the ankles! Ocular clonus and lower-extremity ankle clonus with hyperreflexia define Serotonin Syndrome. In contrast, NMS displays generalized 'lead-pipe' muscular rigidity with hyporeflexia.

drugs.name: Bromocriptine

receptors.clinicalAction: Competitively overcomes neuroleptic blockade in preoptic anterior hypothalamus and striatum, restoring thermal homeostasis
Contributes to central motor stabilization and suppression of extrapyramidal muscular hypertonia.
Ergot-class receptor cross-reactivity; can provoke peripheral vasospasm or nausea at high doses.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Discontinue All Dopamine Blockers Halt all antipsychotics, metoclopramide, and promethazine immediately. Initiate aggressive external cooling and vigorous IV fluid hydration (target urine > 100 mL/h).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer 2.5–5.0 mg three times daily (every 8 hours) orally or crushed via nasogastric tube. Frequently paired with peripheral IV Dantrolene for synergistic rescue.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: If hyperthermia, lead-pipe rigidity, and elevated CK persist, increase by 2.5 mg per dose every 24 hours up to 15–20 mg/day (divided TID; absolute maximum: 45 mg/day).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: Continue 7 Days Past Resolution, then Taper
titrationSchedule.directive: Continue full dose for at least 5 to 7 days after complete resolution of fever and rigidity, then taper over 3 to 5 days. Abrupt cessation triggers fatal rebound NMS! CRITICAL RESUSCITATION HAZARDS & CLINICAL WARNINGS • CRITICAL ROUTE LIMITATION (NO IV FORMULATION): Bromocriptine is available ONLY as oral tablets or capsules; in obtunded NMS patients, tablets must be crushed down a nasogastric tube. • FATAL REBOUND NMS ON ABRUPT STOP: Discontinuing bromocriptine prematurely before central dopamine homeostasis is restored provokes catastrophic rebound NMS with 20% mortality! • Hypotension & Peripheral Collapse: Stimulates vascular dopamine receptors causing pronounced vasodilation; monitor blood pressure closely during IV fluid resuscitation.

clinicalPearls: The Dual NMS Attack: Peripheral + Central: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome involves BOTH peripheral muscle hypermetabolism (calcium dumping) and central dopaminergic deficiency (hypothalamic dysregulation). Combining peripheral IV Dantrolene (blocking RyR1 in muscle) with central oral/NG Bromocriptine (stimulating D2 in brain) produces the fastest documented time to clinical resolution.

The Parkinsonian Withdrawal Trap: NMS can be triggered NOT only by starting an antipsychotic, but also by ABRUPTLY STOPPING a chronic dopaminergic medication (e.g., Levodopa or Pramipexole in a Parkinson's patient). In such cases, emergent re-institution of bromocriptine or levodopa is the specific life-saving cure.

The 7-Day Continuation Rule: Because serum creatine kinase and central dopamine receptors take over a week to recover from neuroleptic toxicity, NEVER stop bromocriptine as soon as the fever breaks. Maintain therapeutic dosing for 7 full days post-normalization of vitals and CK, followed by a stepwise taper.

drugs.name: Physostigmine

adverseFootprint.description: Risk rating: High (Short t½ vs Toxin)

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Verify QRS < 100 ms & Normal PR Screen for cardiac conduction defects. Physostigmine is strictly contraindicated if QRS > 100 ms (TCA overdose). Prepare Atropine 1 mg syringe at the bedside!

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 0.5 mg to 2.0 mg IV over 5 Minutes Administer slow IV push over at least 5 minutes (never push rapidly!). Monitor continuous ECG telemetry and pulse oximetry. Pediatric: 0.02 mg/kg over 5 min.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Assess at 10–15 Minutes (May Repeat 1 mg) Awakening, coherent speech, and sweating confirm diagnostic response. If partial response without cholinergic toxicity, may repeat 1.0–2.0 mg after 15–20 minutes.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: Monitor for 2 to 4 Hours in ED / ICU
titrationSchedule.directive: Because offending anticholinergic toxins (diphenhydramine, benztropine) last 12–24h, delirium often returns within 60 min. Re-dose or bridge with low-dose benzodiazepines. BLACK BOX WARNING & CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATIONS • LETHAL ASYSTOLE IN TRICYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANT (TCA) OVERDOSE: Never administer physostigmine in suspected TCA poisoning or any patient with wide QRS (> 100 ms); induces intractable asystole and death! • Mandatory Bedside Atropine: Always have Atropine (1 mg IV) drawn up at the bedside prior to injection to rapidly reverse excessive cholinergic bradycardia or bronchospasm. • Contraindicated in Bowel/Bladder Obstruction: Contraindicated in mechanical intestinal obstruction or active bronchial asthma.

clinicalPearls: Tertiary vs Quaternary Amines: Neostigmine and Pyridostigmine are quaternary amines that CANNOT penetrate the blood-brain barrier; they only treat peripheral symptoms (myasthenia gravis). Physostigmine is a tertiary amine that freely crosses the blood-brain barrier, making it the ONLY carbamate capable of reversing central anticholinergic delirium.

The 'Dry vs Wet' Diagnostic Confirmation: Central anticholinergic delirium presents with warm, flushed, and bone-dry skin (anhidrosis). Within 5 minutes of successful physostigmine administration, the patient's axillae become noticeably moist and sweating resumes, confirming cholinergic restoration before mental status clears.

Physostigmine vs Benzodiazepines in Anticholinergic Agitation: While benzodiazepines sedate an agitated patient, they do not resolve the delirium and often worsen confusion. Physostigmine reverses the underlying neurochemical defect, rapidly restoring clear cognitive orientation and reducing intubation rates.

drugs.name: Phentolamine

receptors.clinicalAction: Competitively blocks postsynaptic alpha-1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle; triggers intense arterial vasodilation, collapsing
Blocks presynaptic alpha-2 autoinhibitory brakes; uncouples sympathetic feedback, allowing transient reflex norepinephrine

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Continuous Arterial Line / Vital Signs Place patient in monitored ICU/ED resuscitation bay. Connect automated blood pressure cuff cycling every 2 minutes or insert arterial line. Confirm absence of pure beta-blockers.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.dose: Emergency Initial IV Bolus (Tyramine / Cocaine) (Minutes 1 to 5)
titrationSchedule.directive: 5 mg Slow IV Push (Pediatric: 0.1 mg/kg) Administer 5 mg slow IV push over 1 minute. Blood pressure drops precipitously within 60–120 seconds. Target diastolic BP reduction to < 100–105 mmHg.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.dose: Serial Re-Boluses or Continuous Infusion (Minutes 10 to 60)
titrationSchedule.directive: 5 mg IV q5–15m or 0.1–2.0 mg/min Infusion If malignant hypertension recurs as phentolamine clears (t½ ~ 19m), repeat 5 mg bolus every 5–15 minutes, or titrate continuous IV infusion (0.1– 2.0 mg/min) in D5W/NS.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: 5 to 10 mg Subcutaneous Infiltration For norepinephrine/dopamine IV extravasation: infiltrate 5–10 mg in 10 mL saline directly into the blanching, cold ischemic skin using a 25G needle; reverses ischemic necrosis! BLACK BOX WARNING & CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATIONS • STRICT BAN ON PURE BETA-BLOCKERS (UNOPPOSED ALPHA STIMULATION): Never treat MAOI or cocaine hypertensive crises with pure beta-blockers (propranolol); blocking beta-2 vasodilation produces unopposed alpha-1 vasoconstriction, triggering fatal stroke or aortic dissection! • Coronary Artery Disease Caution: Marked reflex tachycardia increases myocardial oxygen demand, predisposing to acute myocardial infarction or arrhythmias. • Renal Artery Stenosis: Profound sudden hypotension can precipitate acute oliguric renal failure.

clinicalPearls: The Unopposed Alpha Trap in Cocaine & MAOI Crises: Medical trainees frequently attempt to treat cocaine or MAOI tachycardia/hypertension with Propranolol or Metoprolol. This is a fatal mistake! Beta-blockade removes beta-2 mediated arteriolar vasodilation while leaving massive alpha-1 vasoconstriction unopposed, causing catastrophic spikes in blood pressure (BP > 240/140 mmHg) and cerebral hemorrhage. Phentolamine is the definitive, specific antidote.

Extravasation Tissue Rescue: When peripheral IV infusions of Norepinephrine (Levophed), Epinephrine, or Dopamine infiltrate into subcutaneous tissues, local alpha-1 vasoconstriction completely halts capillary perfusion, leading to gangrenous necrosis. Subcutaneous infiltration of phentolamine (5–10 mg in 10 mL saline) restores microvascular blood flow within 5 minutes, saving the limb.

Ultra-Short Half-Life Advantage: Phentolamine's brief half-life (19 minutes) is an exceptional safety feature. If excessive dosing drops blood pressure too low, turning off the infusion or waiting 15–20 minutes allows blood pressure to recover promptly without needing emergency vasopressors.

drugs.name: Hydroxocobalamin

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: High-Flow 100% Oxygen + Draw Labs Secure airway, administer 100% oxygen, and draw baseline arterial blood gas, lactate, and cyanide levels before starting infusion (blood will turn bright red).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Two 2.5 g Vials with 100 mL Saline Each Reconstitute each 2.5 g vial with 100 mL of supplied 0.9% normal saline (or lactated Ringer's). Invert or rock vial for 60 seconds; do NOT shake vigorously.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.dose: Emergency Initial 5.0 g IV Infusion (Minutes 3 to 18)
titrationSchedule.directive: 5.0 g IV Infusion Over 15 Minutes Infuse 5.0 g total (both reconstituted 2.5 g vials) intravenously over 15 minutes using dedicated IV line. (Pediatric: 70 mg/kg IV over 15 min, max 5.0 g).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.dose: Clinical Re-Evaluation & Second 5.0 g Dose (Hour 1 Onward)
titrationSchedule.timing: Second 5.0 g IV Over 15 Min to 2 Hours
titrationSchedule.directive: If cardiac arrest, hemodynamic instability, or severe lactic acidosis (lactate > 8–10 mmol/L) persists, administer a second 5.0 g infusion (cumulative maximum dose: 10 g). CRITICAL RESUSCITATION CAUTIONS & LABORATORY ARTIFACTS • LABORATORY SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC INTERFERENCE: Due to intense dark red coloration, hydroxocobalamin causes severe false artifacts on co-oximetry, bilirubin, creatinine, and AST/ALT for 48–72 hours! • Draw Baseline Labs First: Mandatory arterial blood gas, lactate, carboxyhemoglobin, and chemistries must be drawn PRIOR to starting infusion. • Do Not Infuse with Blood Products or Bicarbonate: Hydroxocobalamin is chemically incompatible with blood products, sodium bicarbonate, and diazepam; flush line or use separate lumen.

clinicalPearls: Why Hydroxocobalamin Replaced Nitrites: The old Pasadena Cyanide Antidote Kit contained Amyl Nitrite and Sodium Nitrite, which produced methemoglobinemia (15–30%) to bind cyanide. In enclosed-space house fire smoke inhalation, patients ALREADY suffer from severe carboxyhemoglobinemia (carbon monoxide toxicity). Adding methemoglobinemia destroyed their remaining oxygen-carrying capacity, killing the patient. Hydroxocobalamin creates ZERO methemoglobin and is 100% safe in fire victims.

The Serum Lactate Surrogate Marker: Direct blood cyanide levels take days to return from reference laboratories. Serum lactate is the definitive bedside surrogate: in smoke inhalation victims without major burns, a serum lactate > 8–10 mmol/L has a > 94% sensitivity for toxic blood cyanide (> 40 umol/L), serving as an immediate trigger for Cyanokit administration.

The Burgundy Skin & Urine Phenomenon: Reassure nursing staff and family that deep burgundy-red discoloration of the skin, mucous membranes, and urine is universal, expected, and harmless. It clears spontaneously from the skin within 48–72 hours and from the urine within 2 to 5 weeks as Vitamin B12 is cleared.

receptors.clinicalAction: Blocks striatal cholinergic interneuron signaling, restoring the dopamine-acetylcholine balance disrupted by neuroleptic D2
Cardiac presynaptic muscarinic block; contributes to sinus tachycardia and mild peripheral autonomic effects.
Blocks ciliary, salivary, and detrusor smooth muscle; mediates xerostomia, cycloplegia, constipation, and urinary hesitancy.
Striatal and ventral tegmental modulation; minor contribution to psychotropic alerting and motor coordination.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: 2.5 to 5.0 mg Slow IV / IM Administer slowly over 2-3 minutes. Laryngeal spasm and oculogyric crisis resolve in 3-5 min. May repeat once after 30 min if refractory (max 10 mg/day).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Initiate oral therapy immediately following acute parenteral stabilization to prevent rebound dystonia from depot or long-acting neuroleptics.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard outpatient dose for neuroleptic parkinsonian rigidity, masked facies, and resting tremor. May titrate up to 8-12 mg/day in severe refractory cases.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Taper gradually over 2-4 weeks after antipsychotic dose stabilization or switch to low-EPS atypical. Never stop abruptly to prevent cholinergic storm. CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATIONS & ORGAN TOXICITY WARNINGS • Strictly Contraindicated in Tardive Dyskinesia: Anticholinergic blockade removes the cholinergic brake on hypersensitive striatal dopamine receptors, severely worsening choreic movements and tongue protrusion. • Narrow-Angle Glaucoma & Prostatic Hypertrophy: Muscarinic M3 blockade produces pupil dilation and detrusor paralysis, risking acute angle-closure blindness and complete urinary retention. • Anhidrosis & Fatal Hyperthermia: Inhibits eccrine sweating; exposure to high ambient heat or strenuous exercise can precipitate fatal hyperpyrexia.

clinicalPearls: First-Line Parenteral Antidote for Oculogyric Crisis: Biperiden lactate IV (2.5-5 mg) is the most rapid-acting centrally selective antidote for neuroleptic-induced laryngeal dystonia and oculogyric crisis. Relief of torticollis and breathing difficulty occurs within 3 minutes of IV push.

Rebound Dystonia Trap: Discontinuing biperiden after a single emergency IV dose frequently leads to rebound crisis 12-24 hours later because high-potency neuroleptics (Haloperidol, Fluphenazine) linger in brain tissue far longer than biperiden. Always prescribe 48-72 hours of oral maintenance.

Cognitive Deficits in the Elderly: In patients over 65 years, biperiden carries an Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) score of 3, tripling delirium rates and accelerating dementia. Prefer Amantadine for drug-induced parkinsonism in older adults.

drugs.name: Trihexyphenidyl

receptors.clinicalAction: Suppresses striatal cholinergic interneuron activity, relieving neuroleptic-induced cogwheel rigidity and resting tremor.
Peripheral muscarinic blockade; causes dry mouth, blurry vision, urinary hesitancy, and mild sinus tachycardia.
Inhibits dopamine reuptake; enhances synaptic dopamine availability, which imparts mild mood elevation and abuse liability.
Minimal antihistaminic sedation compared to diphenhydramine; drug has activating/stimulant profile.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 1 mg PO Once Daily with Food
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer single oral dose with breakfast. Evaluates gastrointestinal tolerance and acute central sensitivity (confusion, dizziness) in drug-naive patients.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase to 2 mg with breakfast and lunch. Suppression of mild parkinsonian cogwheeling and akinesia becomes observable within 48-72 hours.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard target for prominent drug-induced parkinsonism and coarse resting tremor. Doses above 10 mg/day require strict monitoring for cognitive slowing.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Gradually taper dose over 2-4 weeks after neuroleptic dose reduction or cessation. Prevents severe cholinergic rebound sweating and akinesia. BLACK BOX WARNING & ABUSE POTENTIAL WARNINGS • Recreational Abuse & Psychological Dependence: Due to mild central dopamine reuptake inhibition, trihexyphenidyl is widely misused for euphoria, auditory hallucinations, and stimulant-like sensations in psychiatric inpatient populations. • Anticholinergic Toxicity Syndrome: High doses provoke central toxic psychosis (restlessness, choreiform movements, picking at air, disorientation, delirium) and peripheral anhidrosis with hyperpyrexia. • Absolute TD Contraindication: Severely worsens Tardive Dyskinesia; never use for abnormal perioral or lingual movements.

clinicalPearls: The 'Artane Euphoria' Phenomenon: Unlike biperiden or benztropine, trihexyphenidyl possesses meaningful DAT reuptake affinity. Patients frequently report an uplifting, stimulating sensation and may feign or exaggerate EPS symptoms to obtain higher doses. Monitor pill counts and pharmacy refill frequency closely.

Take with Meals to Prevent GI Cramping: Trihexyphenidyl can cause nausea and postprandial discomfort if taken on an empty stomach. Administering strictly with meals buffers the gastric mucosa and provides smoother, more sustained absorption.

Deprescribing Mandate After 3 Months: Over 60% of patients who develop early neuroleptic parkinsonism develop striatal tolerance within 2-3 months. Re-evaluate and attempt a gradual taper every 3-6 months rather than leaving patients on indefinite anticholinergic therapy.

drugs.name: Benztropine

receptors.clinicalAction: Potent central muscarinic blockade; rebalances the striatal dopamine-acetylcholine seesaw to eliminate dystonia and
Peripheral parasympathetic inhibition; produces prominent dry mouth, pupil dilation, urinary retention, and anhidrosis.
Inhibits dopamine reuptake into nigrostriatal terminals; synergizes with muscarinic blockade to alleviate akinesia.
Centrally active H1 blockade provides moderate somnolence and sedation, making bedtime administration preferable.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: 1.0 to 2.0 mg IV or Deep IM Administer 1-2 mg IV push or deep IM for acute torticollis, trismus, or oculogyric crisis. Relief typically occurs in 3-5 min (IV) or 15-20 min (IM). Repeat once if needed.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.timing: 1 mg PO BID or 2 mg QHS
titrationSchedule.directive: Continue oral benztropine for 3-7 days following acute emergency treatment to avoid rebound dystonia while high-potency neuroleptic remains tissue-bound.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.timing: 1 to 2 mg PO Twice Daily (or QHS)
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard outpatient maintenance for cogwheel rigidity, masked facies, and resting tremor. Doses up to 4-6 mg/day divided may be used in severe cases.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Attempt periodic taper after 2-3 months of antipsychotic dose stability. Over 70% of patients tolerate withdrawal without EPS recurrence. ORGAN TOXICITY WARNINGS & CRITICAL PRECAUTIONS • Heat Stroke & Anhidrosis Warning: Benztropine impairs thermoregulation by suppressing eccrine sweat glands. In hot environments or during intense physical exertion, fatal hyperpyrexia and heat stroke can occur. • Avoid in Tardive Dyskinesia: Striatal dopamine receptors are supersensitive in TD; benztropine strips away cholinergic counter-regulation, severely worsening involuntary dyskinesias. • Paralytic Ileus: Severe constipation can progress to impaction and fatal paralytic ileus, especially when combined with phenothiazines, TCAs, or clozapine.

clinicalPearls: Once-Daily QHS Dosing Advantage: Because benztropine has a prolonged terminal half-life of 24-36 hours, the entire daily dose (e.g., 2 mg) can be administered at bedtime. This concentrates sedating H1 effects during sleep and reduces daytime anticholinergic complaints.

The Clozapine Interaction Disaster: Never co-prescribe benztropine with Clozapine. Clozapine possesses potent intrinsic antimuscarinic properties at M1/M3/M5; adding benztropine creates severe anticholinergic delirium and fatal gastrointestinal hypomotility (ileus).

Beers Criteria in Geriatric Patients: Benztropine is strongly flagged on the AGS Beers Criteria. In patients >= 65 years, it doubles fall risk, causes urinary retention, and accelerates cognitive decline. Use Amantadine if EPS treatment is unavoidable.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine

receptors.clinicalAction: Blocks hypothalamic histaminergic wake-promoting circuitry; mediates intense sedation, somnolence, and calming of acute panic.
Inhibits striatal cholinergic interneurons; responsible for relieving acute dystonia and extrapyramidal rigidity.
Produces dry mucous membranes, cycloplegia, urinary hesitancy, and mild sinus tachycardia.
Minimal cardiac effect at therapeutic doses; high-dose overdose can prolong QTc and induce ventricular arrhythmias.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: 25 to 50 mg Slow IV / Deep IM Administer 50 mg IV push over 2 minutes (or deep IM) when biperiden/benztropine unavailable. Spasm resolves rapidly in 3-5 min. May repeat once after 20-30 min.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 25 to 50 mg PO Q6-8H Transition to oral formulation for 48-72 hours following emergency resolution to prevent dystonic relapse while offending neuroleptic clears.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: 25 to 50 mg PO at Bedtime Provides nocturnal sedation and mild anticholinergic coverage for mild parkinsonism or akathisia in patients intolerant of beta-blockers.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Diphenhydramine is unsuitable for chronic EPS maintenance due to rapid tolerance to antihistaminic effects and heavy cognitive burden. BLACK BOX WARNING & EMERGENCY SAFETY PRECAUTIONS • Extreme Psychomotor & Driving Impairment: Diphenhydramine causes objective driving impairment comparable to or exceeding blood alcohol concentrations of 0.10%. Strictly warn patients against driving or operating machinery. • Accidental Pediatric Poisoning & Paradoxical Excitation: Overdoses in children provoke severe anticholinergic delirium, hallucinations, hyperthermia, seizures, and death. Paradoxical agitation can occur even at therapeutic doses. • Avoid Long-Term Use in Older Adults: Triples delirium risk and causes urinary retention; listed on Beers Criteria as strongly inappropriate.

clinicalPearls: The Ubiquitous ED Rescue Agent: While biperiden and benztropine are more potent central M1 antagonists, diphenhydramine is universally stocked in every emergency department and crash cart worldwide. When a dystonic patient arrives with severe torticollis or trismus, 50 mg IV diphenhydramine is immediately lifesaving.

Calming the Terrifying Panic of Acute Dystonia: Acute dystonia causes intense subjective horror, as patients feel their neck twisting involuntarily or tongue swelling into the throat. Diphenhydramine's strong H1 sedation rapidly relieves this acute panic state alongside the physical spasm.

Rapid Tachyphylaxis to Sedative Properties: Sedative effects decay dramatically after 3-5 consecutive days of use due to rapid H1 receptor downregulation. Never prescribe diphenhydramine as a long-term sleep aid or chronic EPS prophylactic.

drugs.name: Amantadine

receptors.clinicalAction: Enhances presynaptic vesicular dopamine synthesis, release, and inhibits reuptake, boosting striatal dopaminergic tone.
Exerts neuroprotective and mild antidepressant effects; modulates intracellular calcium mobilization in striatal medium spiny
Active modulation of Muscarinic Receptors (M1-M5) contributes to clinical efficacy and tolerability.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 100 mg PO Once Daily with Breakfast
titrationSchedule.directive: Verify Cockcroft-Gault CrCl > 50 mL/min prior to starting. Administer morning dose with food to evaluate GI tolerance and prevent late-day insomnia.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard target for neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism. Second dose must be taken no later than 2 PM to prevent severe sleep fragmentation.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: For severe parkinsonian akinesia or off-label management of persistent dyskinesia. Doses > 200 mg/day carry elevated risk of hallucinations and confusion.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Adjust by CrCl / Slow Taper If CrCl 30-50 mL/min: 100 mg daily; CrCl 15-29: 100 mg Q48H. Never discontinue abruptly; taper over 1-2 weeks to prevent hyperpyrexic withdrawal crisis. RENAL WARNINGS & CRITICAL NEUROPSYCHIATRIC PRECAUTIONS • Mandatory Renal Dose Reduction: More than 90% is excreted unchanged in urine. Failure to reduce dosage in renal insufficiency leads to toxic drug accumulation, precipitating acute delirium, visual hallucinations, myoclonus, and coma. • Psychosis & Suicidal Ideation Warning: Enhances dopaminergic transmission; can trigger psychotic exacerbations in schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. Monitor closely for depression and suicidality. • Withdrawal Hyperpyrexia Hazard: Abrupt cessation can trigger a life-threatening crisis resembling Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS), with high fever, rigidity, and autonomic instability.

clinicalPearls: The Cognitive-Sparing Antiparkinsonian: Because amantadine has zero anticholinergic activity (ACB = 0), it is the first-line agent of choice for drug-induced parkinsonism in older adults, patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia, where benztropine would trigger delirium.

The '2 PM Cutoff' Rule for Insomnia: Amantadine possesses mild psychostimulant properties. Prescribing the second dose with dinner or at bedtime causes severe insomnia and vivid nightmares. Always schedule doses at 8:00 AM (breakfast) and 1:00 PM (lunch).

Livedo Reticularis is Benign: Up to 10-20% of patients develop reddish-blue, net-like vascular mottling on the lower legs (livedo reticularis) caused by local catecholamine depletion in dermal vessels. It is completely benign, painless, and resolves spontaneously after drug cessation.

drugs.name: Valbenazine

receptors.clinicalAction: Reversibly inhibits presynaptic vesicular monoamine transporter 2; depletes vesicular dopamine stores, dampening striatal
No postsynaptic D2 receptor antagonism; treats tardive dyskinesia without worsening primary parkinsonism or unmasking

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Initiate at 40 mg once daily in the morning or evening without regard to food. Assess for early somnolence or excessive sedation before advancing.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Advance to the recommended target therapeutic dose of 80 mg once daily on Day 8. Quantify reduction in involuntary movements using the AIMS rating scale.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: An intermediate 60 mg capsule is available for patients who experience somnolence at 80 mg but achieve incomplete TD control at 40 mg/day.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: In CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (Ketoconazole), or moderate-severe hepatic impairment, maintain at 40 mg/day. BLACK BOX WARNING & CLINICAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS • Black Box Warning: Depression & Suicidality in Huntington’s Disease: Increases the risk of depression and suicidal thoughts/behavior in patients with Huntington’s chorea. Closely monitor for emergence or worsening of depressive mood. • QTc Interval Prolongation: Causes concentration-dependent prolongation of the QTc interval (mean increase 5-7 ms). Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or arrhythmias. • Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS): Rare cases of NMS-like symptoms reported; immediately discontinue if unexplained hyperthermia or severe rigidity emerges.

clinicalPearls: Single Active Stereoisomer Advantage: Valbenazine is uniquely engineered to deliver only (+)-alpha-HTBZ. Unlike racemic tetrabenazine which contains 4 isomers that hit off-target 5-HT and dopamine receptors, valbenazine has no off-target liability, dramatically reducing rates of dysphoria and parkinsonism.

The 'Once Daily Without Regard to Food' Convenience: Valbenazine absorption is completely independent of meals, and its 20-hour half-life permits consistent once-daily dosing. This provides an enormous adherence advantage in psychiatric patients with irregular meal schedules.

Do Not Stop Antipsychotics Concurrently: When starting valbenazine for TD, do not simultaneously discontinue or abruptly decrease the patient's antipsychotic. Antipsychotic reduction unmasks hidden TD movements, creating the false impression that valbenazine is ineffective.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 6 mg PO Twice Daily with Meals (12 mg/day)
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer 6 mg BID with breakfast and dinner. Taking with meals is mandatory to ensure adequate gastrointestinal absorption and avoid nausea.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Advance dose in 6 mg/day increments every 7 days (e.g., 9 mg BID, then 12 mg BID) guided by reduction in AIMS dyskinesia score and tolerability.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard effective window for tardive dyskinesia. Doses >= 36 mg/day should be divided into two or three administrations taken strictly with food.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: Max 48 mg/day (Max 36 mg in CYP2D6 PM)
titrationSchedule.directive: Maximum ceiling dose is 48 mg/day. If co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (Paroxetine, Fluoxetine) or in poor metabolizers, do not exceed 36 mg/day. BLACK BOX WARNING & PRESCRIBING RESTRICTIONS • Black Box Warning: Depression & Suicidality in Huntington’s Disease: Deutetrabenazine increases the risk of suicidal ideation and depression in Huntington’s patients. Balance chorea suppression against psychiatric risk. • Strict Hepatic Contraindication: Contraindicated in patients with hepatic impairment; decreased first-pass metabolism causes severe drug accumulation. • Concomitant MAOI / Reserpine Prohibition: Contraindicated with MAOIs (allow 14-day washout) and Reserpine (allow 20-day washout) due to risk of serotonin syndrome or profound catecholamine collapse.

clinicalPearls: The Quantum Chemistry of Deuterium: By replacing 6 hydrogen atoms with deuterium, the Carbon-Deuterium bond is strengthened by 6 to 10- fold. This slows CYP2D6 O-demethylation without altering VMAT2 binding, turning an erratic TID drug into a smooth, well-tolerated twice-daily therapy.

The Food Mandate: Deutetrabenazine must never be taken on an empty stomach. Administering with food increases peak concentration (Cmax) by 50% and total exposure (AUC) by ~10%. Remind patients to take doses directly with breakfast and dinner.

Austedo XR Conversion: For patients struggling with twice-daily compliance, an extended-release once-daily tablet (Austedo XR) is available that provides bioequivalent 24-hour coverage when taken in the morning with food.

drugs.name: Tetrabenazine

receptors.clinicalAction: Reversibly inhibits VMAT2; depletes presynaptic vesicles of dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine in striatal terminals.
Off-target monoaminergic binding contributes to depressive dysphoria, insomnia, and orthostatic dizziness.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 12.5 mg PO Once Daily in Morning
titrationSchedule.directive: Initiate at 12.5 mg once daily with food. Screen carefully for personal or family history of depression or suicidal ideation prior to first dose.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase to 12.5 mg with breakfast and dinner. Assess for emerging somnolence, parkinsonian bradykinesia, or worsening dysphoria.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Titrate in 12.5 mg increments weekly up to 50 mg/day divided TID. Doses >= 37.5 mg/day must be split into three divided doses separated by 4-6 hours.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Doses > 50 mg/day are strictly prohibited without CYP2D6 genotyping. In extensive metabolizers, max dose is 100 mg/day (37.5 mg TID max single dose). BLACK BOX WARNING & MANDATORY GENOTYPING GATES • Black Box Warning: Depression & Fatal Suicidality: Tetrabenazine dramatically increases the risk of depression and suicide in patients with Huntington’s chorea. Immediately stop or reduce dose if depressive symptoms emerge. • Mandatory CYP2D6 Genotyping: Prior to prescribing doses > 50 mg/day, the patient MUST be genotyped for CYP2D6. Poor metabolizers cannot exceed 50 mg/day (max single dose 25 mg). • QTc Prolongation & Torsades Hazard: Steep Cmax spikes prolong QTc by up to 8 ms; avoid with other QTc-prolonging drugs (Antipsychotics, Quinidine, Sotalol).

clinicalPearls: The Historical Benchmark vs Modern Alternatives: Tetrabenazine was the first FDA-approved VMAT2 inhibitor, but its non-deuterated racemic formulation produces erratic Cmax spikes and short half-lives requiring TID dosing. Where available, Deutetrabenazine or Valbenazine are overwhelmingly preferred.

The Off-Target D2 Antagonism Trap: Unlike valbenazine, the (-)-beta-HTBZ metabolite of tetrabenazine directly blocks striatal D2 receptors (Ki ~ 150 nM). This can provoke genuine drug-induced parkinsonism, acute dystonia, and akathisia on top of the movement disorder being treated.

The Suicidality Surveillance Protocol: Over 15-20% of patients experience new or worsening depression on tetrabenazine. Provide family members with explicit warning signs and a direct crisis emergency protocol at every clinical visit.

receptors.clinicalAction: Weak central serotonergic antagonism; contributes to anxiolysis and suppression of internal restlessness in akathisia.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.dose: Baseline Vitals & Initial Test Dose (Days 1 to 3)
titrationSchedule.directive: Document baseline pulse and sitting/standing blood pressure. Administer 10 mg PO BID. Verify resting HR >= 60 bpm and systolic BP >= 100 mmHg.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase to 20 mg BID. Significant relief of subjective inner motor restlessness and leg pacing typically manifests within 48 hours of achieving 40 mg/day.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.timing: 20 mg PO TID or 40 mg BID (60–80 mg/day)
titrationSchedule.directive: Target dose for refractory neuroleptic akathisia or severe essential tremor. Monitor resting pulse; hold any dose if HR drops below 55 bpm.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Never stop abruptly. Taper gradually over 1-2 weeks upon antipsychotic stabilization to avoid rebound adrenergic storm, hypertensive surge, or angina. BLACK BOX WARNING & ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATIONS • Black Box Warning: Abrupt Cessation & Cardiac Ischemia: Abrupt withdrawal in patients with occult coronary disease can precipitate severe angina exacerbation, ventricular arrhythmias, and myocardial infarction. • Absolute Asthma Contraindication: Non-selective Beta-2 antagonism causes violent, potentially fatal bronchospasm in patients with asthma or severe COPD. Use cardioselective Metoprolol instead. • Cardiac Conduction Blocks: Strictly contraindicated in sinus bradycardia (HR < 50 bpm), 2nd or 3rd-degree AV block, cardiogenic shock, and decompensated heart failure.

clinicalPearls: Why Lipophilicity is Mandatory for Akathisia: Propranolol is highly lipophilic (logP ~ 2.6) and readily crosses the blood-brain barrier to quiet locus coeruleus hyperactivity. Hydrophilic beta-blockers like Atenolol fail completely in akathisia because they cannot penetrate the central nervous system.

The Bedside '55 / 90' Safety Gate: Instruct nursing staff and outpatients to check pulse and BP prior to each dose. If resting heart rate is below 55 bpm or systolic BP is below 90 mmHg, withhold that dose and re-evaluate.

Masking Hypoglycemic Warning Signs: In diabetic patients taking insulin or sulfonylureas, propranolol blunts sympathetically mediated warning signs of hypoglycemia (tremor, tachycardia, palpitations). Only diaphoresis (sweating) remains unmasked.

drugs.name: Metoprolol

receptors.clinicalAction: Active modulation of Alpha-1 Adrenergic Receptor contributes to clinical efficacy and tolerability.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 25 mg PO BID (Tartrate) or 25-50 mg QD (Succinate)
titrationSchedule.directive: Confirm resting pulse >= 60 bpm and SBP >= 100 mmHg. Initiate 25 mg BID with food to evaluate tolerability and baseline hemodynamic response.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.timing: 50 mg PO BID (Tartrate) or 100 mg QD (Succinate)
titrationSchedule.directive: Advance to 50 mg twice daily with meals. In patients with reactive airway disease, this dose maintains beta-1 cardioselectivity while calming akathisia.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: For persistent motor restlessness. Warning: at total daily doses > 100-150 mg/day, beta-1 selectivity is progressively lost, increasing bronchospasm risk.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Taper gradually over 1-2 weeks upon resolution of akathisia or antipsychotic optimization. Never stop abruptly to prevent rebound hypertension. BLACK BOX WARNING & CARDIORESPIRATORY PRECAUTIONS • Black Box Warning: Abrupt Discontinuation: Abrupt cessation in patients with coronary artery disease can trigger severe angina, ventricular arrhythmias, and myocardial infarction. • Dose-Dependent Loss of Cardioselectivity: At doses > 100 mg/day, metoprolol competitively blocks Beta-2 receptors, which can precipitate severe bronchospasm in asthmatic patients. • Cardiac Conduction Contraindications: Contraindicated in severe bradycardia (HR < 50 bpm), 2nd or 3rd-degree AV block, cardiogenic shock, and decompensated heart failure.

clinicalPearls: The Asthmatic Akathisia Savior: When a patient on a high-potency antipsychotic develops severe neuroleptic akathisia but has comorbid asthma, COPD, or reactive airway disease, non-selective Propranolol is strictly contraindicated. Metoprolol at <= 100 mg/day is the evidence-based beta- blocker of choice.

Tartrate vs Succinate Kinetic Pearls: Metoprolol Tartrate (Lopressor) has a 3-7 hour half-life requiring strict twice-daily administration with meals. Metoprolol Succinate (Toprol XL) provides smooth zero-order 24-hour release, eliminating peak-and-trough blood pressure dips with once-daily dosing.

CYP2D6 Poor Metabolizer Elevation: Metoprolol is cleared predominantly by hepatic CYP2D6. In poor metabolizers (7-10% of Caucasians) or patients taking Fluoxetine/Bupropion, plasma levels rise 3- to 5-fold, increasing bradycardia risk and wiping out cardioselectivity.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: 1.0 to 2.0 mg Slow IV Push (or IM) Administer 1-2 mg IV push over 2 minutes. Assess BFCRS at 30 and 60 minutes. A >= 50% drop in BFCRS or verbalization confirms catatonia. Repeat once if partial.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Divide into three equal doses (e.g., 8 AM, 2 PM, 8 PM). If oral swallowing is impaired, continue IV or deep IM administration. Continuous telemetry monitoring.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Titrate upwards by 2-4 mg/day until complete motor and verbal normalization is achieved. Refractory or malignant cases may require 20-30 mg/ day under ICU care.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Maintain full therapeutic dose for 3-6 months. Taper extremely slowly (no faster than 0.5-1.0 mg every 1-2 weeks) to prevent catastrophic catatonic relapse. BLACK BOX WARNING & CATATONIA RESUSCITATION PRECAUTIONS • Black Box Warning: Opioid Co-Administration: Concomitant use with opioids results in profound sedation, fatal respiratory depression, and coma. Reserve co-use strictly for monitored ICU settings. • Catastrophic Rebound on Abrupt Cessation: Rapid tapering or abrupt stoppage triggers immediate, severe catatonic relapse, malignant hyperthermia, status epilepticus, and death. • Propylene Glycol Toxicity with IV Infusion: Continuous high-dose IV lorazepam infusions (> 1 mg/kg/day) can cause propylene glycol diluent toxicity (metabolic acidosis, acute renal injury).

clinicalPearls: The 'Paradoxical Awakening' Marker: In non-catatonic individuals, 2 mg of IV lorazepam induces heavy sedation and sleep. In a catatonic patient, 2 mg IV causes dramatic awakening: mutism disappears, frozen postures dissolve, and the patient converses freely. This confirms the diagnosis.

The 'Under-Dosing' Catatonia Pitfall: The most common error in catatonia management is prescribing standard anxiolytic doses (e.g., 0.5-1 mg PO daily). Catatonia involves profound cortical GABA-A down-regulation requiring robust receptor saturation; effective doses typically range from 8 to 16 mg/day.

Clean Hepatic Safety Profile: Lorazepam undergoes direct 3-glucuronidation via UGT2B7 to an inactive metabolite, completely bypassing hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes. It remains safe in cirrhosis, hepatitis, and in elderly patients with hepatic decline (part of the 'OTL' safe benzodiazepine triad).

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Baseline BFCRS Score on Empty Stomach Document full 23-item BFCRS score. Ensure patient has not eaten for >= 2 hours. Have airway support and suction ready at bedside.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 10 mg PO (or 5–10 mg Sublingual) Administer Zolpidem 10 mg PO (crushed via NG tube if mutism/stupor prevents swallowing) or 10 mg sublingual tablet (Edluar) under the tongue.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Evaluate at 30, 60, and 120 Minutes Observe for sudden motor liberation, normal speech, and resolution of waxy flexibility. A positive response confirms catatonia beyond any diagnostic doubt.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: High-Dose Lorazepam or Bilateral ECT Because awakening is transient (lasts 2-4 hours), immediately transition patient to standard IV Lorazepam titration protocol or emergency bilateral ECT. BLACK BOX WARNING & COMPLEX SLEEP BEHAVIOR PRECAUTIONS • Black Box Warning: Complex Sleep Behaviors: Zolpidem can provoke complex sleep behaviors including sleepwalking, sleep-driving, preparing meals, and making phone calls while not fully awake. Discontinue immediately if these occur. • Transient Duration Trap: Zolpidem’s short half-life (𝑡{1 2} ≈2 −3ℎ) means catatonic stupor and mutism will return within 2 to 4 hours. It is a diagnostic challenge agent, NOT an effective standalone maintenance therapy. • Avoid with Alcohol & CNS Depressants: Severe, fatal respiratory depression occurs when combined with alcohol, opioids, or sedating neuroleptics.

clinicalPearls: The 'Lazarus Awakening' Phenomenon: In deep catatonic stupor, administration of 10 mg oral zolpidem produces a dramatic paradoxical awakening within 20-30 minutes: previously mute and rigid patients sit up, converse normally, eat, and express relief. Symptoms return as plasma levels fall 2-3 hours later.

Diagnostic Utility When Lorazepam Fails: Up to 15-20% of catatonic patients fail a standard 2 mg lorazepam challenge. In these equivocal cases, a 10 mg zolpidem challenge frequently succeeds, definitively confirming catatonia and avoiding misdiagnosis as dementia or refractory psychosis.

The Sublingual (SL) Delivery Trick: In patients with severe mutism and clenched teeth (trismus), swallowing oral tablets is impossible. Placing a 5-10 mg sublingual zolpidem tablet (Edluar) directly into the buccal mucosa permits rapid transmucosal absorption without requiring NG tube insertion.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer 0.125 mg PO 2 to 3 hours before anticipated bedtime. Taking with a light snack minimizes initial area postrema nausea.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase to 0.25 mg daily if restless legs symptoms, nighttime motor restlessness, or sleep fragmentation persist. Screen for early excessive daytime sleepiness.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Target maximum for Restless Legs Syndrome. Doses > 0.5 mg/day carry dramatically higher rates of augmentation and impulse control disorders.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Taper and Switch to Alpha-2-Delta If augmentation develops (symptoms advancing into afternoon or arms), do NOT raise dose. Taper pramipexole slowly and cross-titrate to Gabapentin enacarbil or Pregabalin. BLACK BOX WARNING & IMPULSE CONTROL PRECAUTIONS • Severe Impulse Control Disorders: Up to 15-20% of patients develop devastating compulsive behaviors: pathological gambling, compulsive shopping, hypersexuality, and binge eating. Explicitly warn family members. • Sudden Sleep Attacks: Patients can fall asleep suddenly without warning while engaging in daily activities, including driving motor vehicles, causing fatal motor vehicle accidents. • Dopamine Agonist Withdrawal Syndrome (DAWS): Rapid tapering can provoke a severe withdrawal state: profound anhedonia, panic attacks, suicidal ideation, and diaphoresis refractory to levodopa.

clinicalPearls: The 'Augmentation' Trap in RLS: Over 50-70% of RLS patients treated long-term with dopamine agonists develop augmentation: symptoms occur earlier in the day (e.g., 2 PM instead of 10 PM), become more intense, and spread to the upper extremities. The catastrophic mistake is increasing the dose, which accelerates the vicious cycle. The correct move is weaning off pramipexole and switching to an Alpha-2-Delta ligand.

The Powerful Antianhedonic D3 Signature: Due to 7-fold preferential affinity for mesolimbic D3 receptors over D2, pramipexole has demonstrated robust efficacy in treatment-resistant bipolar depression and unipolar anhedonia (at doses of 1.0 to 2.0 mg/day), far beyond its motor indications.

Renal Clearance Dependency: Over 90% is eliminated unchanged via the kidneys. In patients with CrCl < 50 mL/min, dosing frequency must be reduced (e.g., 0.125 mg every other day) to prevent toxic hallucinations and orthostatic syncope.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer 0.25 mg 1 to 3 hours before sleep with food. Pairing strictly with meals reduces intense initial nausea from area postrema D2 stimulation.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase to 0.5 mg daily for the remainder of Week 1. Evaluate therapeutic relief of leg restlessness and assess for morning orthostasis.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase by 0.5 mg/week to target range of 1-2 mg/day. A second divided dose in late afternoon may be required if symptoms emerge before dinner.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Never exceed 4 mg/day for RLS. If augmentation occurs, taper gradually by 0.25-0.5 mg weekly to prevent dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome (DAWS). BLACK BOX WARNING & CYP1A2 INTERACTION PRECAUTIONS • Impulse Control Behaviors Warning: Clinicians must actively query patients and families regarding compulsive gambling, shopping, sexual preoccupation, and binge eating at every visit. • CYP1A2 Interactions & Smoking Status: Ropinirole is metabolized exclusively by CYP1A2. Tobacco smoke induces CYP1A2, lowering drug levels by 30%. Smoking cessation or CYP1A2 inhibitors (Ciprofloxacin, Fluvoxamine) double plasma levels, causing severe emesis and hallucinations. • Postural Hypotension & Syncope: Induces peripheral vasodilation; check sitting and standing BP before titrating.

clinicalPearls: Managing the Brutal Area Postrema Nausea: Ropinirole stimulates D2 receptors in the area postrema (chemoreceptor trigger zone), causing intense nausea during early titration in over 30% of patients. Taking with a protein-rich snack or co-prescribing Trimethobenzamide (avoid metoclopramide or prochlorperazine which block striatal D2 and provoke severe dystonia) prevents discontinuation.

The Tobacco Smoke Pitfall: A patient well-controlled on ropinirole 1 mg who suddenly enters a smoke-free inpatient psychiatric unit loses CYP1A2 induction. Within 72 hours, ropinirole levels spike, provoking severe nausea, orthostatic collapse, and delirium.

Shift to Alpha-2-Delta Ligands: Recent International RLS Study Group (IRLSSG) guidelines recommend Alpha-2-Delta calcium channel ligands (Pregabalin, Gabapentin) over dopamine agonists as first-line chronic therapy, due to the > 50% long-term risk of ropinirole-induced augmentation.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Start at 25 mg (quarter of 100 mg tablet) strictly at bedtime. Mandatory precaution to prevent incapacitating acute first-dose vertigo and vomiting.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: 100 to 125 mg PO at Bedtime Increase by 25-50 mg every 3-4 days to reach 100-125 mg QHS. Evaluates tolerance to daytime sedation and cerebellar coordination.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.timing: 250 mg PO BID to TID (500–750 mg/day)
titrationSchedule.directive: Standard therapeutic window for disabling essential tremor. Doses above 250 mg/day should be divided into morning, afternoon, and bedtime administrations.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Serum Phenobarbital Level & Taper Monitor phenobarbital levels (target 10-25 mcg/mL for tremor). Taper slowly over months if discontinuing to prevent severe barbiturate withdrawal seizures. BLACK BOX WARNING & METABOLIC ENZYME INDUCTION • The Violent ‘First-Dose Phenomenon’: Up to 20% of patients experience an acute neurotoxic reaction (violent vertigo, intractable vomiting, ataxia, prostration) within 2-4 hours of the first dose if started at standard 250 mg doses. Always start at 25 mg! • Life-Threatening Barbiturate Withdrawal: Abrupt cessation can precipitate severe barbiturate withdrawal: status epilepticus, autonomic delirium, hyperthermia, and death. • Massive CYP Induction: Potently induces CYP3A4, CYP2C9, and UGTs; dramatically lowers blood levels of oral contraceptives, DOACs, lamotrigine, and antipsychotics.

clinicalPearls: The 'Quarter-Tablet' Rule for Essential Tremor: Starting a patient on a standard 250 mg tablet will lead to immediate abandonment of the drug in nearly a quarter of patients due to severe nausea, dizziness, and collapse. Prescribe 100 mg tablets and instruct the patient to take 1/4 tablet (25 mg) at bedtime, advancing by 25 mg weekly.

Dual Active Mechanism in Tremor: While primidone is converted to phenobarbital, unmetabolized parent primidone has direct intrinsic antitremor properties independent of phenobarbital. In fact, tremor suppression is often observed within 24-48 hours, long before phenobarbital reaches steady state.

Co-Prescription of Folate and Vitamin D: Chronic primidone accelerates hepatic breakdown of vitamin D (causing osteomalacia and osteoporosis) and inhibits intestinal absorption of folic acid (provoking megaloblastic anemia). Always co-prescribe 1 mg folic acid and 2000 IU vitamin D3.

titrationSchedule.directive: Advance to 1,000 mg PO BID (2,000 mg/day) if partial-onset or generalized seizures persist. Monitor for emerging mood lability or explosive irritability.

titrationSchedule.directive: Maximum FDA-approved maintenance dose for refractory epilepsy. In patients exhibiting severe behavioral toxicity, consider adding Pyridoxine (B6).

Pre-existing psychiatric illness triples this risk. • Mandatory Renal Adjustment: Excreted largely unchanged by the kidneys; failure to reduce dosage in renal insufficiency provokes toxic drug accumulation, profound somnolence, and confusion. • Abrupt Withdrawal Hazard: Abrupt cessation can precipitate breakthrough status epilepticus. Always taper gradually.

clinicalPearls: The 'Keppra Rage' Mitigation Strategy: Levetiracetam-induced irritability and hostility ('Keppra rage') can often be reversed by co-administering Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) at 50 to 100 mg PO BID. Pyridoxine facilitates GABA synthesis, calming hyper-glutamatergic behavioral storms without compromising seizure control.

The Gold-Standard Anticonvulsant for Polypharmacy: Because levetiracetam undergoes blood enzymatic hydrolysis and renal excretion with zero CYP450 involvement, it produces zero drug-drug interactions with antipsychotics, antidepressants, mood stabilizers, or immunosuppressants.

Post-TBI Seizure Prophylaxis Window: In traumatic brain injury, levetiracetam 500-1000 mg IV/PO BID is equivalent to phenytoin in preventing early post-traumatic seizures (first 7 days), with vastly superior tolerability and zero need for therapeutic blood level monitoring.

titrationSchedule.dose: Restart Rule After Lapsed Dosing (Safety Rule)
titrationSchedule.timing: Restart at 25 mg if Stopped > 4 Days
titrationSchedule.directive: If a patient misses doses for more than 4-5 consecutive days (> 5 half-lives), all immune tolerance is lost. The entire titration must be restarted from 25 mg! BLACK BOX WARNING & DRUG INTERACTION MANDATES • Black Box Warning: Serious Skin Rashes (SJS / TEN): Fatal cases of Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis and Stevens-Johnson Syndrome occur; risk is dramatically increased by exceeding initial doses or co-prescribing with valproate. Discontinue at first sign of rash. • Valproate Interaction (UGT Inhibition): Valproate doubles lamotrigine half-life to > 60 hours; lamotrigine doses MUST be reduced by >= 50% (starter kit: Blue blister pack). • Oral Contraceptives (UGT Induction): Estrogen-containing OCPs induce glucuronidation, slashing lamotrigine levels by 50%. Doses must be doubled, and adjusted during the pill-free week.

clinicalPearls: The '4-Day Lapsed Dosing' Rule: If a patient on 200 mg/day stops taking lamotrigine for 5 or more days, you CANNOT simply resume their 200 mg dose. Their immune tolerance has completely reset, and resuming at full dose carries an extreme risk of lethal Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. Titration must restart at 25 mg daily.

The Estrogen Withdrawal Seizure Spike: In women taking combined oral contraceptives, lamotrigine levels drop by 50% during active hormone weeks. During the inactive placebo week, estrogen clears and lamotrigine levels double, risking severe toxicity (diplopia, ataxia) or withdrawal seizures.

Differentiating Benign Exanthema from SJS: About 10% of patients develop a harmless morbilliform rash. However, if the rash involves mucosal membranes (lips, mouth, eyes, genitals), facial swelling, high fever, or skin peeling, it is an immediate emergency: discontinue permanently and transfer to a burn unit.

For mild-to-moderate Tourette syndrome or chronic motor tics, Clonidine (or Guanfacine) is the preferred first-line therapy because it quiets prefrontal locus coeruleus noradrenergic firing with zero TD risk.

The Transdermal Patch Compliance Secret: In children with Tourette syndrome or autism who fight swallowing pills, the weekly transdermal patch (Catapres-TTS) is transformative. It provides steady, zero-order delivery over 7 days, eliminating daytime sedation peaks and compliance battles.

Managing the Rebound Crisis: If a patient abruptly stops clonidine and presents in hypertensive crisis, immediately administer oral clonidine 0.2 mg stat followed by 0.1 mg hourly until BP normalizes, or administer IV Phentolamine/Labetalol to block the catecholamine surge.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Baseline ECG, K+, Mg2+ & CYP2D6 Genotyping Obtain baseline 12-lead ECG, serum potassium, magnesium, and CYP2D6 genotype. Do NOT initiate if QTc > 450 ms in males or > 460 ms in females.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.timing: 1 to 2 mg PO Once Daily at Bedtime
titrationSchedule.directive: Administer 1-2 mg QHS. Evaluates tolerance and early extrapyramidal sensitivity. Co-prescribe an oral anticholinergic (Biperiden/Benztropine) if EPS emerges.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.timing: Increase by 1-2 mg Every Other Day
titrationSchedule.directive: Advance slowly to target 4 to 8 mg/day. Perform repeat 12-lead ECG at steady state. Withhold dose and reduce if QTc interval increases by > 60 ms.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.timing: Max 10 mg/day (Max 4 mg in CYP2D6 PM)
titrationSchedule.directive: Absolute ceiling is 10 mg/day (or 0.2 mg/kg/day). In CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, do NOT exceed 4 mg/day (or 0.05 mg/kg/day). Serial ECGs mandatory. BLACK BOX WARNING & MANDATORY CARDIAC GATES • Black Box Warning: Sudden Unexpected Death & Fatal Torsades: Pimozide prolongs the QTc interval in a dose-dependent manner, provoking fatal ventricular arrhythmias and Torsades de Pointes. Strict ECG monitoring required. • Mandatory CYP2D6 Genotyping Gate: Doses > 4 mg/day are strictly prohibited without prior CYP2D6 genotype testing. In poor metabolizers, pimozide accumulates to toxic levels, causing fatal arrhythmias. • Contraindicated with CYP Inhibitors & Macrolides: Strictly contraindicated with CYP3A4 inhibitors (Ketoconazole, Clarithromycin), CYP2D6 inhibitors (Paroxetine, Fluoxetine), and any QTc drugs.

clinicalPearls: The Monothematic Delusion Specialist: Pimozide remains uniquely famous in neuropsychiatry as the most effective pharmacological treatment for Delusional Parasitosis (Ekbom syndrome: fixed false belief of insect infestation under the skin). Its ultra-pure D2/D3 blockade silences the aberrant tactile hallucination loops driving the somatic delusion.

The Strict '4 mg CYP2D6 Gate': The FDA black box warning explicitly dictates that CYP2D6 genotyping is required before exceeding 4 mg/day (or 0.05 mg/kg/day in children). In poor metabolizers, plasma concentrations spike 4- to 8-fold, turning a standard 6 mg dose into a lethal pro- arrhythmic hazard.

Extreme EPS Vigilance Required: Because pimozide lacks anticholinergic, antihistaminic, or alpha-blocking properties, its D2 blockade is unbuffered. Over 40% of patients develop acute dystonia, severe cogwheel rigidity, or akathisia during early titration. Keep Biperiden or Benztropine immediately available.

drugs.name: Zuranolone

receptors.clinicalAction: Active modulation of Monoamine Transporters (SERT/DAT/NET) contributes to clinical efficacy and tolerability.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.timing: 50 mg PO Once Daily with Fatty Evening Meal
titrationSchedule.directive: Instruct patient to take exactly 50 mg in the evening with a meal containing 400-1000 calories and >= 25% fat. Taking on an empty stomach slashes absorption by > 75%.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Maintain 50 mg (or Cut to 40 mg if Sedated) Evaluate for excessive sedation or morning grogginess. If daytime somnolence is incapacitating, reduce dose to 40 mg PO once daily for the remainder of the 14-day course.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Patient completes the 14-day course. Do not extend therapy beyond 14 days. Clinical remission is typically evident by Day 3 to 15, with therapeutic gains maintained post-treatment.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Monitor for Relapse / Ongoing Therapy Evaluate Hamilton Depression (HAM-D) scores. If PPD recurs months later, a repeat 14-day course may be considered, or standard oral SSRI maintenance initiated. BLACK BOX WARNING & DRIVING IMPAIRMENT PRECAUTIONS • Black Box Warning: Severe CNS Depression & Impaired Driving: Zuranolone causes profound sedation and psychomotor slowing. Patients must be warned NOT to drive a motor vehicle or operate complex machinery for at least 12 hours after every evening dose. • Mandatory Fatty Meal Requirement: Co-administration with a fat-containing meal increases Cmax by 3.5-fold and AUC by 4.3-fold. Taking without food leads to therapeutic failure. • Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Can cause fetal harm if taken during pregnancy; highly effective non-hormonal contraception required during treatment and for 1 week after last dose.

drugs.foodRequirement: Take once daily in the evening with a fat-containing meal for optimal absorption.
clinicalPearls: The Postpartum Nighttime Caregiver Mandate: Because zuranolone causes intense sedation during the night, clinicians must verify that a partner, family member, or night nurse is present in the home to manage nighttime infant feedings and emergencies for the 14-day duration.

The 'Fatty Meal' Secret: Emphasize to the patient that a light salad or apple is insufficient. Zuranolone requires fat (e.g., avocado, cheese, whole milk, peanut butter, or meat) to achieve therapeutic systemic absorption. Taking it on an empty stomach results in subtherapeutic blood levels.

Lactation Transfer Profile: Zuranolone transfers into human breast milk in minimal amounts, with an estimated Relative Infant Dose (RID) of ~ 0.3%. However, due to its recent approval and sedative potency, infant monitoring for excessive sleepiness, poor feeding, or hypotonia is strongly advised.

drugs.name: Brexanolone

receptors.clinicalAction: Directly mimics third-trimester allopregnanolone levels; restores tonic inhibition in limbic and frontostriatal circuits.
Potentiates phasic inhibitory chloride currents, providing rapid relief of severe postpartum despair, anxiety, and suicidal ideation.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 1
titrationSchedule.directive: Admit to REMS-certified facility. Place dedicated IV line and continuous pulse oximetry with audible alarm. Initiate infusion at 30 mcg/kg/hr.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 2
titrationSchedule.directive: Increase rate to 60 mcg/kg/hr. Re-assess patient consciousness, sedation score (RASS), and pulse oximetry q2h. Check for excessive somnolence.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 3
titrationSchedule.directive: Advance to full target rate of 90 mcg/kg/hr for a 28-hour plateau. If excessive somnolence occurs at any point, immediately reduce rate to 60 mcg/ kg/hr.

titrationSchedule.title: STEP 4
titrationSchedule.directive: Taper to 60 (4h), then 30 (4h), then Stop Reduce to 60 mcg/kg/hr for Hours 52-56, then 30 mcg/kg/hr for Hours 56-60, then discontinue. Total infusion duration is exactly 60 hours. BLACK BOX WARNING & STRICT REMS PROTOCOL MANDATES • Black Box Warning: Excessive Sedation & Sudden Loss of Consciousness: Brexanolone causes sudden loss of consciousness in 4% of patients. Available strictly through a restricted REMS program. • Mandatory Continuous Pulse Oximetry: Patients must have continuous pulse oximetry monitoring with an audible alarm throughout the entire 60-hour infusion. • Childcare Restrictions: Patients must not be the sole caregiver of their infant or any children during the infusion; a companion must be present during any infant interaction.

clinicalPearls: The 'Lazarus Effect' in Postpartum Despair: Brexanolone produces the most rapid, profound antidepressant response documented in clinical psychiatry: women with severe, suicidal postpartum depression experience near-complete remission within 24 to 48 hours of starting the infusion.

The Cyclodextrin (SBECD) Renal Caveat: Brexanolone is solubilized using sulfobutylether beta-cyclodextrin (SBECD), which is eliminated exclusively by the kidneys. Avoid in patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min) due to risk of toxic cyclodextrin accumulation.

Lactation During Infusion: Brexanolone transfers into breast milk at extremely low levels (RID < 1.3%). However, due to maternal sedation during the infusion, breastfeeding should be paused and milk pumped/discarded or stored, resuming fully after the 60-hour infusion concludes.
